chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Sulayman ibn Zayd, the freedman of Tirbal, and others, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The charity of one Dirham in Kufah is counted as two hundred Dirhams elsewhere, and two Rak'ahs prayed in it are counted as one hundred Rak'ahs.

key_terms.الْكُوفَة: Kufah, a city in Iraq with high spiritual merit
key_terms.دِرْهَم: A silver coin used as a unit of currency
key_terms.نَفَقَة: Charity or expenditure given in the path of God

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward multiplier for charity and prayer in Kufah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the superior merit of Kufah, stating that a single Dirham given as charity there is equivalent to two hundred Dirhams elsewhere, and two units of prayer (Rak'ahs) performed there are rewarded as if one had prayed one hundred units. This specific multiplier reflects the historical significance of Kufah as a center of early Shia scholarship and the Imams' residence, where the spiritual weight of acts is amplified due to the presence of the Ahl al-Bayt and the concentration of faithful followers. Such narrations in *Kamil al-Ziyarat* serve to encourage consistent devotion and charitable giving in this sacred locale, reinforcing its status as a spiritual hub distinct from other cities.
